newsitem.title: USA: Moyco to plead guilty on foot-powder charge.
newsitem.headline: Moyco to plead guilty on foot-powder charge.

text.p: Moyco Technologies Inc said on Wednesday it agreed to plead guilty and pay a fine of at least $175,000 on federal criminal charges that it failed to maintain required quality-control and stability-testing procedures for foot powder it sold the U.S. government.

The company said it agreed to plead guilty to federal charges of distributing adulterated drugs and mail fraud in connection with the Itch-Away power it sold the government from 1992 to 1996. The powder was for use by soldiers.
A Moyco corporate officer, whose name was not released, also will plead guilty to mail fraud from delivering the powder, the company said.
The possibility of civil restitution remains, Moyco said.
The range of the possible fine in the criminal case runs from $175,000 to $700,000. The hearing has not been set.
Moyco said its own investigation determined that the foot powder sold to the government was safe and effective.
Moyco, which makes precision abrasives and dental supplies among other materials, no longer makes foot powder, the company said. Moyco shares closed at 4-1/2 on Wednesday, down 1 on the day.
